title: Prefetch orchestration and transport variance notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working notes doc for experiments exploring how proactive KV-cache prefetch orchestration interacts with NCCL transport selection and PCIe host staging across mixed batch/seq workloads. Goal is to find heuristics that reduce tail latency for long-context streaming without regressing median throughput for short-context high-qps workloads.

Background/context:
- We observed tail spikes when a small fraction of requests have long contexts and trigger KV cache population across shards; these spikes correlate with NCCL transport changes (rc_v2 vs ud) and sudden PCIe host staging bursts.
- Earlier logs: saw 200–600 ms tail variance during 99.9th percentile for a 4-GPU pipeline shard. Suspected contributing factors: aggressive prefetch causing bus contention, RPCs queued on host, and NCCL fallback/transport renegotiation.

Testbed summary:
- HW: 4x A100-SXM GPUs per node, 2 nodes connected via HDR200, dual-rail IB with RoCE paths; PCIe Gen4 x16 for host-GPU.
- SW: NCCL 2.18, CUDA 12.2, driver 545.x, serving-runtime branch: pr/prefetch-orch/experiment (PR 1874).
- Models: 13B mixed-precision decoder-only (sharded TP=2/PP=2), sequence lengths: 64(short), 2048(long).
- Workloads: 95% short single-turn queries, 5% long-context streaming sessions (multi-chunk). Arrival processes: Poisson for short, bursty for long sessions.

Experiment plan & variants (high level):
1) Baseline: no prefetch beyond immediate request; default NCCL transport.
2) Aggressive prefetch: prefetch full KV for predicted continuation on session start.
3) Staggered prefetch: prefetch at chunk boundaries with randomized jitter across replicas to avoid synchronized bursts.
4) Prefetch with transport pinning: prefer RC transport + force small-message aggregation before NCCL ops.
5) Host-staging rate-limiter: throttle DMA host copies per-device during prefetch windows.

Metrics captured:
- p50/p95/p99/p99.9 latency for token generation and first-token latency for streaming
- GPU utilization, PCIe read/write throughput, IB link utilization (per-rail), NCCL op counts and transport type breakdown
- Queue depth at host staging threads and DMA submission times
- End-to-end error/retry counts and NCCL fallback events

Commands / instrumentation notes (scratch):
- perf counters: nvidia-smi dmon / nvprof (deprecated) -> use nvtx + Nsight Systems captures
- NCCL logging: export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL=2 for GDR tracing
- host staging logs: /var/log/serving/host-staging.log (produce JSON lines)
- sample tracing slice: ./bin/serving_journal --trace session_id=XXXX --from 2025-07-12

Preliminary observations (runs 2025-07-11 through 2025-07-16):
- Baseline: stable median latency (p50 ~ 12 ms per token) but p99.9 spikes up to ~520 ms coinciding with long-session arrivals. NCCL logs show occasional transport fallback events minutes after a long-session starts.
- Aggressive prefetch: reduces p99 for long sessions by ~18% but increases overall p99.9 due to synchronized host-staging bursts when multiple replicas prefetch same prefixes. PCIe read throughput shows microbursts (see Nsight sample A).
- Staggered prefetch (randomized jitter 5–50 ms across replicas): preserves long-session improvements while largely eliminating synchronized PCIe microbursts; p99.9 reduced by ~120 ms vs aggressive prefetch.
- Transport pinning: forcing RC eliminates some fallback churn but increased average NCCL latency for short messages (small allreduce overhead). Net effect: small regression in p50 for short queries (~+1.6 ms) but lower p99.9 for mixed workload.
- Host-staging rate-limiter: effective in smoothing PCIe bandwidth, but if limit set too low (>20% below observed average) we see throughput regression for long-session generation.

Micro-profiling notes (important traces):
- Trace #A (2025-07-13 03:12): aggressive prefetch, 3 replicas started on same session -> host-staging queue depth spike to 384, PCIe read plateau at 96% for 120 ms, NVLINK mostly idle due to host-centric transfers.
- Trace #B (2025-07-14 14:05): staggered prefetch with 30 ms jitter -> host queue depth peaks ~48, PCIe read bursts smaller and spread, NVLINK used more for inter-GPU sharing after prefetch completes.
- NCCL events in traces: look for repeated ‘transport negotiate’ event sequences; correlate timestamps with host-staging queue drain.

Hypotheses / interpretation:
- Synchronized prefetch is the major root cause of microbursts that overwhelm PCIe/host DMA and indirectly triggers NCCL transport renegotiation (timing-dependent).
- A modest per-replica jitter plus soft rate-limits provides the best tradeoff for mixed workloads.
- For single-node multi-GPU setups with heavy host staging, it's better to favor intra-node NVLINK aggregation (batching small KV transfers into NVLINK transfers) rather than simultaneous PCIe reads.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need to measure impact of enabling GDR for host staging (NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL=something) in our infra, especially on the RDMA-enabled interconnect. (Action: Diego to run GDR vs no-GDR runs, JIRA-RT-5127)
- Explore design where only one replica does full prefetch and shares prepared KV over NVLINK to other local replicas (master-replica prefetch). Evaluate cross-replica trust/consistency implications.
- Tune jitter distribution: currently uniform 5–50 ms; try exponential/backoff-based jitter and compare tail behavior.
- Add synthetic microbench that issues prefetch-only load to observe pure PCIe/host saturation thresholds instead of mixed compute.
- Investigate small-message NCCL optimization (aggregator layer) to reduce overhead when forcing RC/transport pinning.

Actionable immediate steps (next 2 sprints):
- Implement staggered prefetch as opt-in policy in runtime (feature flags) with configurable jitter and rate-limits. (Owner: Jinwoo, PR link above)
- Add host-staging telemetry: sample-size-limited histograms in Console for host DMA queue depth and PCIe burst length. (Owner: Maya)
- Run repeatable perf harness with seed-controlled arrival patterns for statistical significance; store traces under s3://redwood-experiments/prefetch/2025-07. (Owner: Asha)

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider prefetch cost amortization: if we detect a long-session after first chunk, model can switch to ‘coordinated prefetch slow-mode’ where prefetches are throttled to match generation rate.
- Potential integration with router: route long-session prefetches to less-loaded nodes/regions to spread PCIe pressure.
- If we add master-replica prefetching, need to handle eviction and versioning of KV layers to avoid stale state during rollouts.

References & attachments:
- Nsight captures: s3://redwood-traces/prefetch/traceA.nsight (Trace A), traceB.nsight
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1874 (prefetch orchestration prototype)
- Confluence: Prefetch Playbook (internal): https://confluence.redwood.local/display/RT/Prefetch+Playbook
